inlines.v: FULL-WINGED, adjective 1. Having complete wings or large strong wings. 2. Ready for flight; eager. FULL, verb transitive [Latin fullo. Gr. that is, a crowd, a throng. foul and defile are probably of the same family.] To thicken cloth in a mill. This is the primary sense: but in practice, to full is to mill; to make compact; or to scour, cleanse and thicken in a mill.
